passage: Coastal dunes protect inland areas, yet damaged dunes cannot always be rebuilt by simply adding sand. Loose sand may blow away before plants establish roots. Some restoration teams install low, flexible barriers that slow the wind without blocking it completely. Sand settles around the barriers, creating small ridges where native grasses can take hold. The method requires monitoring because a barrier placed in the wrong direction can redirect erosion. Its value lies in working with local movement rather than attempting to freeze a changing coastline.
